headline: Wall Street claws back losses as US inflation stays high and Brent rebounds
paragraphs: US stocks recovered much of Wednesday’s early slide but were still lower heading into the final hours of trade. At 5:17 am Sydney, the S&P 500 was down 0.71% at 7,150.24, after dipping below 7,000. The Nasdaq-100 had been down 2.64% at 25,521.55 at 4:16 am; Nasdaq’s later reading showed it down 1.16% at 25,911.01. These are intraday readings, not closes. Renewed selling in chip and AI shares and fresh tariff worries weighed on sentiment ahead of Thanksgiving.

The US data gave investors little reason to expect relief on interest rates. The Fed’s preferred inflation measure, the PCE price index, rose 3.8% in the year to October, with core PCE at 3.3%. At the same time, US third-quarter growth was revised up from 3.4% to a 4.3% annualised rate. Stronger growth alongside above-target inflation makes it harder to argue for lower rates.

In Australia, the ASX 200 last closed down 0.4% at about 8,692 on Wednesday, with miners and banks weighing on the index after annual inflation climbed to 4.9%. The Australian dollar’s initial inflation-driven jump didn’t stick. It recovered some ground overnight to 66.15 US cents at 4:42 am Sydney but remained 0.36% below MarketWatch’s previous close.

Gold and oil went different ways. Kitco’s spot gold bid was down 0.50% at US$3,537.30 a troy ounce around 6 am Sydney. January Brent reversed its earlier fall, reaching US$93.74 a barrel in a delayed 4:47 am quote, 2.56% above Tuesday’s settlement. The next US cash session is skipped for Thanksgiving, and Friday’s New York session closes early at 5 am Saturday Sydney time.
